The bug was that `Progress.stop()` was outputting a blank line on non-interactive consoles even when the `Progress` instance was created with `disable=True`. This happened because `Progress.stop()` did not check the `disable` flag, whereas `Progress.start()` did.

I have updated `rich/progress.py` to wrap the logic in `stop()` with `if not self.disable:`, ensuring symmetry with `start()`.

Verified the fix with a reproduction script that captured output to a buffer using a non-interactive console.

Summary of changes:
- Modified `rich/progress.py`: Added `if not self.disable:` check in `Progress.stop()` method.
